question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

All in all, he had the more splendid collection of antique paintings ever.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. most splendid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "ever" indicates a comparison with all other collections, so the superlative degree is required — "the most splendid collection ... ever", not the comparative "the more splendid".

◦ Correct: All in all, he had the most splendid collection of antique paintings ever.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "more splendider" is a double comparative — always incorrect.

• Option 3 "splendid" (positive degree) cannot follow "the ... ever" in a superlative sense.

• Option 4 "splendidest" is wrong because long adjectives like "splendid" form the superlative with "most", not "-est".

NOTE

• Superlative markers: "the ... ever", "of all", "in the world/class". Long adjectives: more + adjective (comparative), the most + adjective (superlative) — more splendid / the most splendid.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The company plans to expand its operations into global markets soon.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Restrict.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Expand" means to increase in size, scope or extent; to spread out. (विस्तार करना)

• Its antonym is "restrict", meaning to limit or confine within bounds. (सीमित करना)

◦ Example: The new rules restrict the company's operations to the domestic market.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Spread" and Option 4 "Diversify" are close in sense to "expand" (synonyms), not antonyms.

• Option 1 "Eliminate" (to remove completely) does not convey the opposite of "expand" (the opposite of expanding is limiting, not removing).

NOTE

• Synonyms of expand: enlarge, extend, spread, widen, grow. Antonyms: restrict, contract, shrink, reduce, curtail.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom from the options given below.

To show the white feather
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To act cowardly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to show the white feather" means to act in a cowardly manner; to show fear or cowardice. (कायरता दिखाना)

◦ Example: The soldier showed the white feather and fled from the battlefield.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The idiom comes from cock-fighting: a gamecock with a white feather in its tail was considered to be of inferior breed and likely to run away from a fight.

• Options 2, 3 and 4 do not convey cowardice; Option 4 "to act bravely" is the opposite.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "show a clean pair of heels" (run away), "get cold feet" (lose courage), "lion-hearted" (very brave), "white elephant" (a costly but useless possession) — do not confuse the "white" idioms.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My brother trains young girls at the football academy, whereas I gets a handsome salary to teach mathematics at the same place.
option_3: to teach mathematics at the same place
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. I gets a handsome salary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The pronoun "I" is first person singular and always takes the plural form of the verb in the present tense — "I get", never "I gets". The "-s" form (gets) is used only with third person singular subjects (he/she/it).

◦ Correct: ... whereas I get a handsome salary to teach mathematics at the same place.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "My brother trains young girls" is correct — third person singular "brother" + "trains".

• "at the football academy, whereas" and "to teach mathematics at the same place" contain no error.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: I/we/you/they + base verb (get, go, play); he/she/it + verb + s/es (gets, goes, plays). "Whereas" is used to contrast two clauses.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Reverent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Respectful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Reverent" means showing deep respect and admiration, especially towards something sacred. Its closest synonym is "respectful". (श्रद्धालु / आदरपूर्ण)

◦ Example: The devotees stood in reverent/respectful silence before the shrine.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Rushed" (hurried), Option 2 "Important" (significant) and Option 3 "Related" (connected) are unrelated in meaning.

• Do not confuse "reverent" (respectful) with "reverend" (a title for a clergyman) or "relevant" (connected with the matter).

NOTE

• Word family: revere (verb — to respect deeply), reverence (noun), reverent (adjective). Synonyms: respectful, devout, deferential. Antonyms: irreverent, disrespectful, impious.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
option_1: An unexpected power failure completely foiled the plan of the team.
option_2: An unexpected power failure completely foiled a plan of a team.
option_3: A unexpected power failure completely foiled the plan of a team.
option_4: An unexpected power failure completely foiled an plan of the team.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. An unexpected power failure completely foiled the plan of the team.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Unexpected" begins with a vowel sound, so it takes the article "an" — "an unexpected power failure".

• "The plan of the team" correctly uses the definite article for a specific plan of a specific team.

◦ Correct: An unexpected power failure completely foiled the plan of the team.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "a plan of a team" makes both nouns vague where a specific plan/team is meant.

• Option 3 wrongly uses "A" before the vowel sound of "unexpected".

• Option 4 wrongly uses "an" before "plan" (consonant sound).

NOTE

• Article rule: "a/an" depends on the sound, not the letter — an hour, an MLA, a university, a one-rupee coin. "Foil" means to defeat/thwart a plan. (विफल करना)

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

The bread was drier and stale.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. dry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The two adjectives joined by "and" must be in the same degree (parallel). Since "stale" is in the positive degree, the first adjective must also be positive — "dry and stale", not "drier and stale".

◦ Correct: The bread was dry and stale.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• There is no comparison in the sentence (no "than"), so the comparative "drier"/"much drier" is wrong.

• Option 3 "driest" (superlative) needs "the" and a comparison among many.

• Option 4 "more drier" is a double comparative — always incorrect.

NOTE

• Parallelism: adjectives joined by "and" should match in degree — "dry and stale", "taller and stronger". Degrees of dry: dry – drier – driest.

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

After their disagreement, they decided to saparate their belongings and part ways.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. separate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "separate", meaning to divide or set apart. (अलग करना)

◦ Correct: ... they decided to separate their belongings and part ways.

• Spelling key: SE + PA + RATE — remember "there is a rat in separate".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "seperate", "seprete" and "seprate" are all misspellings; "seperate" (with "e" in the middle) is one of the most commonly misspelt words in English.

NOTE

• Word family: separate (verb/adjective), separation (noun), separately (adverb), separable (adjective). Frequently tested spellings: separate, definitely, occurrence, accommodation, necessary.

question:
One of the four underlined words in the given sentence is incorrectly spelt. Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

Let us appreciate, support and contribute our might to the promotional efforts of the comunity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. comunity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Comunity" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "community" (with double "m"), meaning a group of people living in the same place or sharing common interests. (समुदाय)

◦ Correct: ... the promotional efforts of the community.

• Spelling key: COM + MU + NITY — double "m".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "appreciate" (to value/praise), "promotional" (relating to publicity) and "contribute" (to give a share) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Words with double "m": community, committee, commission, accommodate, communicate, recommend (one "c", double "m").

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The scientist conducted a series of experiments to _______ his hypothesis.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. verify.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Verify" means to check or prove that something is true or correct. A scientist conducts experiments to verify (test/confirm) his hypothesis. (सत्यापित करना)

◦ Correct: The scientist conducted a series of experiments to verify his hypothesis.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The blank after "to" needs a verb; Option 1 "variation" (noun — a change), Option 2 "variable" (noun/adjective — a changing quantity) and Option 3 "vague" (adjective — unclear) do not fit grammatically or in meaning.

NOTE

• Word family: verify (verb), verification (noun), verifiable (adjective). Synonyms: confirm, validate, substantiate, authenticate. A "hypothesis" is a proposed explanation that is tested by experiments.

question: Select the option that has an error in the use of phrasal verb.
option_1: Why does she break out with all her near and dear ones?
option_2: To earn a significant profit, you are advised to deal in electronic items.
option_3: Clean up the mess in the kitchen. It is unhygienic.
option_4: We look forward to seeing you during the event.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Why does she break out with all her near and dear ones?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb for ending a relationship is "break up with", not "break out with". "Break out" means to start suddenly (war/fire/disease broke out) or to escape.

◦ Correct: Why does she break up with all her near and dear ones?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "deal in" (to trade in/sell something) is correctly used — deal in electronic items.

• Option 3 "clean up" (to make a place clean and tidy) is correct.

• Option 4 "look forward to + -ing" (to await eagerly) is correct — look forward to seeing.

NOTE

• Common "break" phrasal verbs: break up (end a relationship), break out (start suddenly/escape), break down (stop working/collapse), break into (enter forcibly), break off (end abruptly).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Johannes Gutenberg invented the first printing press that could print thousands of ______________ a day. This made books cheaper and information ______________ widely available.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. pages; more.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After "thousands of", a plural countable noun is needed — "thousands of pages". A printing press prints pages.

• The second blank needs the comparative "more widely available" — the press made information more widely available than before.

◦ Correct: ... could print thousands of pages a day. This made books cheaper and information more widely available.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "sheet" and Option 3 "leaf" are singular and cannot follow "thousands of"; "much/many" cannot modify the adverb "widely" here.

• Option 4 "sides; most" — "sides" does not collocate with printing, and "most widely" (superlative) does not suit the comparison implied.

NOTE

• "Thousands of/hundreds of/millions of" + plural noun. Johannes Gutenberg (Germany, c. 1440) invented the movable-type printing press — a fact often asked in GK too.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Although she is usually / rude with everyone, / she behaved nice / with all of us today.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. she behaved nice.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "behaved" must be modified by an adverb, not an adjective. "Nice" is an adjective; the adverb is "nicely". So the segment should be "she behaved nicely".

◦ Correct: Although she is usually rude with everyone, she behaved nicely with all of us today.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Although she is usually", "rude with everyone" and "with all of us today" are grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Adjectives qualify nouns/pronouns; adverbs modify verbs — behave nicely, sing sweetly, drive carefully. Most adverbs of manner are formed by adding "-ly" to the adjective (nice → nicely).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word.

I cannot see without my glasses.
option_1: A device used to correct the defects of vision
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A device used to correct the defects of vision.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the sentence "I cannot see without my glasses", the word "glasses" means spectacles — a device (pair of lenses) worn to correct defects of vision. (चश्मा)

◦ Example: He wears glasses because he is short-sighted.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Glass" (singular) can mean a container for drinking or the material, but "glasses" with "see" clearly refers to spectacles.

• Options 2, 3 and 4 ignore the context of seeing/vision.

NOTE

• Words with different singular/plural meanings: glass (material/tumbler) – glasses (spectacles); scale (measure) – scales (weighing machine); custom (habit) – customs (import duty).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

They all felt that the movie was truly captivating and unforgettable.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. repugnant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Captivating" means extremely attractive, charming and holding one's attention. (मनमोहक)

• Its antonym is "repugnant", meaning extremely distasteful; causing strong dislike or disgust. (घृणित / अप्रिय)

◦ Example: The audience found the vulgar scenes repugnant.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "tantalising" (teasing with something desirable) and Option 4 "charismatic" (charming, attractive) are close to "captivating" — synonyms, not antonyms.

• Option 2 "relatable" (easy to identify with) is not an opposite.

NOTE

• Synonyms of captivating: enchanting, fascinating, mesmerising, alluring. Antonyms: repugnant, repulsive, revolting, offensive.

question:
Rectify the sentence by selecting the correct spelling from the options.

All the political parties of India appaer lost in the physical exercise of fighting elections.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Appear.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "appear" (double "p", then "-ear"), meaning to seem; to come into sight. (प्रतीत होना / दिखाई देना)

◦ Correct: All the political parties of India appear lost in the physical exercise of fighting elections.

• Spelling key: AP + PEAR — "appear" contains the word "pear".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Apeear", "Aapear" and "Apearr" are all misspellings.

NOTE

• Word family: appear (verb), appearance (noun), apparent (adjective), apparently (adverb). Antonym: disappear. Note the single "p" in "apart" but double "p" in "appear/apparent".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I long from travel outside the country, dreaming of adventures among the towering Alps and basking in the turquoise waters of the Caribbean.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. long to travel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "long" (to desire strongly) is followed by either "to + base verb" (long to travel) or "for + noun" (long for a holiday). "Long from" is incorrect.

◦ Correct: I long to travel outside the country, dreaming of adventures among the towering Alps ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "long at travel" uses a wrong preposition.

• Option 3 "long for travelling" is unidiomatic here — "long for" takes a noun (long for peace), and the intended sense is the infinitive of purpose.

• Option 4 "long for travelled" is grammatically impossible (past participle after "for").

NOTE

• "Long to + V1" = to yearn/desire strongly to do something. (लालायित होना) Similar patterns: yearn to go, crave for success, aspire to become.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Triumph
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Failure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Triumph" means a great victory, success or achievement. (विजय / जीत)

• Its antonym is "failure" — lack of success; defeat. (असफलता)

◦ Example: The mission ended in failure, not in triumph.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Lapse" (a small error/slip or passage of time), Option 3 "Attentiveness" (alertness) and Option 4 "Delay" (lateness) are not opposites of victory.

NOTE

• Synonyms of triumph: victory, success, conquest, win. Antonyms: failure, defeat, loss. Idiom: "triumph over adversity" — to succeed despite difficulties.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

She is someone who always discourages our enthusiasm; therefore, we have decided to keep our distance from her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. a wet blanket.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a wet blanket" means a person who spoils other people's fun or discourages their enthusiasm. It exactly substitutes "someone who always discourages our enthusiasm". (रंग में भंग डालने वाला व्यक्ति)

◦ Correct: She is a wet blanket; therefore, we have decided to keep our distance from her.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a nine days' wonder" — something that attracts attention for a short time and is soon forgotten.

• Option 2 "a fish out of water" — a person in an uncomfortable/unfamiliar situation.

• Option 4 "a cash cow" — a business or product that gives steady profit.

NOTE

• Similar expressions: "killjoy", "spoilsport", "party pooper" — all denote a person who dampens others' enjoyment.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A building where animals are butchered
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Abattoir.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "abattoir" is a building/place where animals are butchered (slaughtered) for food — a slaughterhouse. (कसाईखाना / वधशाला)

◦ Example: Strict hygiene rules apply inside an abattoir.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Decanter" — a glass container into which wine is poured before serving.

• Option 3 "Burrow" — a hole dug by an animal (like a rabbit) as a dwelling.

• Option 4 "Cemetery" — a place where the dead are buried.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: aviary (a place for birds), apiary (bees), aquarium (fish), kennel (dogs), stable (horses), granary (grain), abattoir (slaughterhouse).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Goddess Shailputri is the first form of Goddess Durga, who is worshipped ____(1)___ Navaratri. In this form, she is worshipped as the daughter of ___(2)__ Himalayas. She is the goddess ___(3)____ nature and is adorned with flowers. She ___(4)__ a bull and holds a trident in one hand and a lotus flower in another. During Navaratri, nine different forms of Durga are worshipped. Durga is a ___(5)__, ___(6)___, ___(7)___ deity who is also known as Adishakti—the energy that manifested to create the universe.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. during.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "during" is used to show that something happens within a particular period or event — the goddess is worshipped during Navaratri (i.e., throughout the festival period). (के दौरान)

◦ Correct: ... Goddess Durga, who is worshipped during Navaratri.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "by" (agent/means), Option 2 "to" (direction) and Option 3 "among" (in the middle of more than two) do not express the time period of the festival.

• The passage itself later says "During Navaratri, nine different forms of Durga are worshipped", confirming the choice.

NOTE

• "During" + noun of time/event (during the festival, during the war); "for" + duration (for nine days); "while" + clause (while the festival was on).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Goddess Shailputri is the first form of Goddess Durga, who is worshipped ____(1)___ Navaratri. In this form, she is worshipped as the daughter of ___(2)__ Himalayas. She is the goddess ___(3)____ nature and is adorned with flowers. She ___(4)__ a bull and holds a trident in one hand and a lotus flower in another. During Navaratri, nine different forms of Durga are worshipped. Durga is a ___(5)__, ___(6)___, ___(7)___ deity who is also known as Adishakti—the energy that manifested to create the universe.

Select the most appropriate article to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The definite article "the" is always used before the names of mountain ranges — "the Himalayas", "the Alps", "the Andes".

◦ Correct: ... she is worshipped as the daughter of the Himalayas.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "A/an" (indefinite articles) cannot be used with a proper noun like "Himalayas", and "no article" is wrong because plural mountain-range names require "the".

NOTE

• "The" is used with: mountain ranges (the Himalayas), rivers (the Ganga), oceans/seas (the Pacific), deserts (the Sahara), island groups (the Andamans), holy books (the Gita) and newspapers (The Hindu). Single peaks usually take no article (Mount Everest).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Goddess Shailputri is the first form of Goddess Durga, who is worshipped ____(1)___ Navaratri. In this form, she is worshipped as the daughter of ___(2)__ Himalayas. She is the goddess ___(3)____ nature and is adorned with flowers. She ___(4)__ a bull and holds a trident in one hand and a lotus flower in another. During Navaratri, nine different forms of Durga are worshipped. Durga is a ___(5)__, ___(6)___, ___(7)___ deity who is also known as Adishakti—the energy that manifested to create the universe.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "of" shows relation/possession — "the goddess of nature" means the goddess associated with (presiding over) nature. (की देवी)

◦ Correct: She is the goddess of nature and is adorned with flowers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options "at" (place/point), "with" (accompaniment/instrument) and "around" (surrounding) do not express the possessive/appositive relation required here.

• Compare: god of rain, goddess of wealth (Lakshmi), goddess of knowledge (Saraswati).

NOTE

• "Of" is the most common preposition of relation/belonging: the capital of India, the leg of the table, the goddess of nature.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Goddess Shailputri is the first form of Goddess Durga, who is worshipped ____(1)___ Navaratri. In this form, she is worshipped as the daughter of ___(2)__ Himalayas. She is the goddess ___(3)____ nature and is adorned with flowers. She ___(4)__ a bull and holds a trident in one hand and a lotus flower in another. During Navaratri, nine different forms of Durga are worshipped. Durga is a ___(5)__, ___(6)___, ___(7)___ deity who is also known as Adishakti—the energy that manifested to create the universe.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. rides.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The whole passage describes the goddess in the simple present tense (is worshipped, is adorned, holds), because it states permanent/universal facts. To maintain tense consistency, the blank needs the simple present "rides".

◦ Correct: She rides a bull and holds a trident in one hand and a lotus flower in another.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "was riding" (past continuous), Option 2 "had ridden" (past perfect) and Option 4 "rode" (simple past) break the present-tense narration of the passage.

• The parallel verb "holds" (simple present) in the same sentence confirms "rides".

NOTE

• Universal truths, habitual actions and descriptions of deities/characters are written in the simple present tense. Subject "She" (third person singular) takes "rides" with "-s".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Goddess Shailputri is the first form of Goddess Durga, who is worshipped ____(1)___ Navaratri. In this form, she is worshipped as the daughter of ___(2)__ Himalayas. She is the goddess ___(3)____ nature and is adorned with flowers. She ___(4)__ a bull and holds a trident in one hand and a lotus flower in another. During Navaratri, nine different forms of Durga are worshipped. Durga is a ___(5)__, ___(6)___, ___(7)___ deity who is also known as Adishakti—the energy that manifested to create the universe.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blanks number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. powerful; radiant; Indian.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When several adjectives come before a noun, they follow the standard order of adjectives: opinion/quality → physical quality → origin/nationality → noun. Hence "a powerful (quality), radiant (physical quality), Indian (origin) deity".

◦ Correct: Durga is a powerful, radiant, Indian deity who is also known as Adishakti ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• In options 1, 2 and 4, the nationality adjective "Indian" wrongly appears before quality adjectives; adjectives of origin always come closest to the noun.

NOTE

• Royal order of adjectives (OSASCOMP): Opinion – Size – Age – Shape – Colour – Origin – Material – Purpose + noun. Example: a beautiful big old round red Indian wooden dining table.

question: Who was the court poet of king Harshavardhana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Banabhatta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Banabhatta was the court poet (Asthana Kavi) of king Harshavardhana (r. 606–647 CE) of the Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) dynasty. He wrote "Harshacharita" (the biography of Harsha) and the Sanskrit prose romance "Kadambari". (बाणभट्ट — हर्षवर्धन के दरबारी कवि)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Harshavardhana ruled from Kannauj (earlier Thanesar); the Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) visited India during his reign.

• Harsha himself wrote three Sanskrit plays — Nagananda, Ratnavali and Priyadarshika.

• Kalidasa was associated with Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya); Ravikirti was the court poet of Chalukya king Pulakeshin II (Aihole inscription); Vatsabhatti composed the Mandsaur inscription.

NOTE

• Harsha was defeated by Pulakeshin II on the banks of the Narmada. He organised religious assemblies at Kannauj and Prayag.

question: As per Article 181, the ___________ can not preside while a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration in State Legislative Assembly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Speaker.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 181 of the Constitution provides that the Speaker (or the Deputy Speaker) of the State Legislative Assembly shall not preside over a sitting while a resolution for his own removal from office is under consideration. (अनुच्छेद 181 — अध्यक्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Speaker of a Legislative Assembly is elected by its members and can be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Assembly, after 14 days' notice (Article 179).

• The corresponding provision for the Lok Sabha Speaker is Article 96.

• The Chairman/Deputy Chairman relate to the Legislative Council (Articles 182–185); the Advocate General (Article 165) is the highest law officer of the state.

NOTE

• During such removal proceedings, the Speaker may speak and take part in the proceedings and can vote in the first instance, but not preside and not use a casting vote.

question: In 1928, who among the following wrote the Congress Party's Nehru Report, a future constitution for independent India, based on the granting of dominion status?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Motilal Nehru.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Nehru Report (1928) was prepared by a committee headed by Motilal Nehru (with his son Jawaharlal Nehru as secretary). It was the first major Indian attempt to draft a constitutional framework for India, demanding Dominion Status. (मोतीलाल नेहरू — नेहरू रिपोर्ट, 1928)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The report was a response to the challenge of the Secretary of State Lord Birkenhead and the all-white Simon Commission (1927).

• It recommended dominion status, joint electorates, fundamental rights, and universal adult franchise.

• Muhammad Ali Jinnah rejected it and put forward his "Fourteen Points" (1929).

• The younger leaders (Jawaharlal Nehru, Subhas Chandra Bose) wanted Purna Swaraj instead of dominion status; the Lahore Session (1929) adopted Purna Swaraj as the goal.

NOTE

• 26 January 1930 was celebrated as the first Independence Day (Purna Swaraj Day); later the Constitution commenced on 26 January 1950.

question: The Patkai hills are part of the ____________ mountains.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Purvachal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Patkai hills (Patkai Bum) are part of the Purvachal — the Eastern Hills of India, which are the eastward extension of the Himalayas along India's border with Myanmar. (पटकाई पहाड़ियाँ — पूर्वांचल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Purvachal comprises the Patkai Bum, Naga hills, Manipur hills and Mizo (Lushai) hills, running through Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram.

• These hills are made of strong sandstones and are covered with dense forests.

• The Western Ghats (Sahyadri) run along the west coast; the Eastern Ghats are discontinuous hills along the east coast; the Karakoram lies in the trans-Himalayan region (K2, the highest peak of India).

NOTE

• The Purvachal hills form the physiographic link between the Himalayas and the Arakan Yoma of Myanmar.

question: In which of the following events did India get its first individual Olympic gold medal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shooting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's first individual Olympic gold medal was won by Abhinav Bindra in Shooting — the 10 m Air Rifle event at the 2008 Beijing Olympics. (अभिनव बिंद्रा — निशानेबाज़ी, बीजिंग 2008)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India's second individual Olympic gold was won by Neeraj Chopra in Javelin Throw at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics (held in 2021).

• India's first individual Olympic medal (post-independence) was K. D. Jadhav's bronze in wrestling (Helsinki, 1952); Karnam Malleswari (weightlifting bronze, Sydney 2000) was the first Indian woman Olympic medallist.

• India's earlier Olympic golds were all in hockey (8 team golds, including 6 in a row 1928–1956).

NOTE

• Abhinav Bindra received the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2001-02) and the Padma Bhushan (2009). His autobiography is "A Shot at History".

question: The term 'foot fault' is associated with which of the following games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tennis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The term "foot fault" is associated with Tennis (Lawn Tennis). It occurs when the server's foot touches the baseline or the court before the ball is struck during a serve — the serve is then declared a fault. (फुट फॉल्ट — टेनिस)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other tennis terms: ace, deuce, advantage, let, volley, smash, grand slam, tie-breaker, love.

• The four Grand Slam tournaments: Australian Open, French Open (Roland Garros), Wimbledon and US Open.

• Terms of other games: Hockey — penalty corner, bully, scoop; Basketball — dribble, dunk, free throw; Archery — bullseye, end, quiver.

NOTE

• "Foot fault" also exists in volleyball and cricket's no-ball has a similar foot-position logic, but in standard SSC answer keys it is matched with Tennis.

question:
Calculate the revenue receipts from the following information.

Revenue deficit= 2.80% of GDP Revenue expenditure= 10.80% of GDP
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.00.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts.

• Therefore, Revenue Receipts = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Deficit = 10.80% − 2.80% = 8.00% of GDP.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Revenue receipts are receipts that neither create a liability nor reduce assets — tax revenue (income tax, GST, excise) and non-tax revenue (interest, dividends, fees).

• Revenue expenditure is expenditure that does not create assets — salaries, pensions, subsidies, interest payments.

• Other deficits: Fiscal Deficit = Total expenditure − Total receipts (excluding borrowings); Primary Deficit = Fiscal deficit − Interest payments; Effective Revenue Deficit = Revenue deficit − Grants for creation of capital assets.

NOTE

• A high revenue deficit shows the government is borrowing even to meet its consumption (day-to-day) expenditure — considered the least desirable deficit.

question: When a large amount of carbon dioxide dissolves in a water body, the water becomes acidic because of the formation of which of the following acids?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carbonic acid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When carbon dioxide (CO₂) dissolves in water, it forms "carbonic acid (H₂CO₃)", which makes the water acidic:

◦ CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃

• This is why increasing CO₂ causes ocean acidification. (कार्बोनिक अम्ल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Carbonic acid is a weak acid; soda water/aerated drinks contain dissolved CO₂ as carbonic acid.

• Option 1 "Carboxylic acids" are organic acids with the –COOH group (e.g., acetic acid).

• Option 3 "Carbolic acid" is phenol (used as a disinfectant); "Carbamic acid" is NH₂COOH.

• Ocean acidification harms corals and shell-forming organisms by reducing carbonate availability.

NOTE

• Acid rain, by contrast, is mainly caused by sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄) and nitric acid (HNO₃) formed from SO₂ and NOₓ; normal rain is slightly acidic (pH ≈ 5.6) due to carbonic acid.

question: Which programme, that was introduced in the year 2000-2001, aims to offer homes, drinking water, primary education and basic healthcare in rural areas?
option_3: The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana (PMGY)" was introduced in 2000-2001 with the objective of achieving sustainable human development at the village level — focusing on rural shelter (homes), drinking water, primary education, primary health and nutrition, and rural electrification. (प्रधानमंत्री ग्रामोदय योजना — 2000-01)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY), launched 25 December 2000, provides all-weather road connectivity to unconnected villages — roads only, not homes/health/education.

• Option 1 PM-KISAN (2019) gives ₹6,000 per year income support to farmer families.

• Option 4 Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (2017) is a pension scheme for senior citizens (60+) run through LIC.

NOTE

• PMGY allocated Additional Central Assistance to states for five basic minimum services — a precursor to later missions like PMAY (housing) and Jal Jeevan Mission (drinking water).

question: Which of the following institutes/projects is declared as a masterpiece of oral and intangible heritage of humanity by UNESCO in May 2001?
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Project to support Kuttiyattam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In May 2001, UNESCO declared "Kuttiyattam (Kutiyattam), the Sanskrit theatre of Kerala" a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity — the first Indian art form to receive this recognition; the national project supporting Kuttiyattam is associated with it. (कुटियाट्टम — केरल का संस्कृत रंगमंच)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kutiyattam is one of the oldest living theatre traditions (about 2,000 years old), traditionally performed in temple theatres called Koothambalams by the Chakyar community, combining Sanskrit drama with Kerala's local traditions.

• Other Indian entries on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list include: Vedic chanting, Ramlila, Ramman, Mudiyettu, Kalbelia dance, Chhau dance, Buddhist chanting of Ladakh, Sankirtana of Manipur, Yoga, Nawrouz, Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja of Kolkata (2021) and Garba of Gujarat (2023).

NOTE

• The "Masterpieces" proclamation (2001, 2003, 2005) was later merged into the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity under the 2003 UNESCO Convention.

question: Select the INCORRECT pair of molecule/formula units and their molar mass from the following.
solution_text:
The correct answer is HNO3 - 62.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The pair "HNO₃ – 62" is incorrect. The molar mass of nitric acid (HNO₃) = 1 (H) + 14 (N) + 3 × 16 (O) = 63 g/mol, not 62.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• CH₄ (methane) = 12 + 4 × 1 = 16 g/mol — correct.

• NaCl (sodium chloride) = 23 + 35.5 = 58.5 g/mol — correct.

• HCl (hydrochloric acid) = 1 + 35.5 = 36.5 g/mol — correct.

• Atomic masses to remember: H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, Na = 23, Cl = 35.5, S = 32, Ca = 40.

NOTE

• Molar mass is the mass of one mole (6.022 × 10²³ particles — Avogadro's number) of a substance, expressed in g/mol. The molar mass in grams numerically equals the molecular mass in atomic mass units (u).

question: In animal cells, the breakdown of very long chain fatty acids through ꞵ-oxidation is conducted by which of the following organelles?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Peroxisome.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In animal cells, the breakdown of very long chain fatty acids (VLCFAs) by β-oxidation is carried out by the "peroxisomes". They shorten the very long chains, after which mitochondria complete the oxidation. (परॉक्सिसोम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Peroxisomes are small, single-membrane-bound organelles containing oxidative enzymes such as catalase, which breaks down toxic hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) into water and oxygen.

• Mitochondria ("powerhouse of the cell") perform β-oxidation of normal (short/medium/long chain) fatty acids and produce ATP.

• Ribosomes synthesise proteins; the Golgi apparatus packages and dispatches materials.

NOTE

• Defective peroxisomal β-oxidation causes disorders like adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD). Peroxisomes were discovered by Christian de Duve, who also discovered lysosomes.

question: How many cities have been selected to be developed as sustainable and responsible destinations as per the Swadesh Darshan 2.0 scheme launched by the Union Ministry of Tourism in January 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 30.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the revamped "Swadesh Darshan 2.0" scheme of the Union Ministry of Tourism (January 2023), about 30 cities/destinations were selected to be developed as sustainable and responsible tourist destinations. (स्वदेश दर्शन 2.0 — 30 शहर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The original Swadesh Darshan Scheme (2014-15) was a central sector scheme for developing theme-based tourist circuits (e.g., Ramayana, Buddhist, Coastal, Desert, Eco, Heritage and North-East circuits).

• Swadesh Darshan 2.0 shifts from circuit-based development to destination-based, sustainable and responsible tourism, following the idea of "vocal for local".

• Related scheme: PRASHAD (Pilgrimage Rejuvenation And Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive) for pilgrimage sites.

NOTE

• Tourism themes for SSC: Ministry of Tourism campaigns — "Incredible India", "Dekho Apna Desh"; Swadesh Darshan is 100% centrally funded.

question: Which of the following architectural elements is excluded from the construction sites of the Indus Valley Civilisation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iron Slabs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Iron slabs" were not used in the Indus Valley Civilisation — the Harappans belonged to the Bronze Age (Chalcolithic) and had no knowledge of iron. Their constructions used sun-dried and baked (burnt) bricks and gypsum mortar. (सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता — लोहे का ज्ञान नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Harappan bricks were of the standard ratio 4 : 2 : 1 (length : breadth : thickness).

• The Harappans used copper, bronze, gold and silver, but not iron; iron appears in India around 1000 BCE (later Vedic period, e.g., Painted Grey Ware sites).

• Famous structures: Great Bath (Mohenjo-daro) — made watertight with baked bricks, gypsum mortar and bitumen; Granary; dockyard at Lothal.

NOTE

• Indus cities show grid-pattern town planning, covered drains and citadel/lower-town division — all achieved without iron tools.

question: In the 1991 Census, which state was the highest in rank in terms of literacy rate and held higher than the national average of literacy rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the 1991 Census, Kerala ranked first among Indian states in literacy rate (about 89.8%), far above the national average of about 52.2%. (केरल — साक्षरता में प्रथम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kerala has retained the top literacy rank in every census; in the 2011 Census its literacy rate was 94.0% (national average 74.04%).

• In 2011, the lowest literacy was in Bihar (61.8%); Kottayam/ Ernakulam districts of Kerala are among the most literate districts.

• Literacy rate (Census definition): percentage of population aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding.

NOTE

• Kerala also leads in Human Development Index, sex ratio (1,084 females per 1,000 males in 2011) and life expectancy among Indian states.

question: Which organelle contains ribosomal RNA and is involved in the production of ribosomes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nucleolus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "nucleolus" is a dense, spherical structure inside the nucleus that contains ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and is the site of ribosome (subunit) production/biogenesis. (केंद्रिका — राइबोसोम का निर्माण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The nucleolus is a non-membrane-bound structure; a nucleus may contain one or more nucleoli.

• Ribosomes ("protein factories") are assembled from rRNA + proteins; they may float free in the cytoplasm or attach to the rough endoplasmic reticulum.

• The Golgi apparatus packages and secretes materials; the nucleus as a whole stores DNA and controls the cell.

NOTE

• Ribosomes: prokaryotes have 70S ribosomes; eukaryotes have 80S (S = Svedberg unit). Cells making lots of protein have prominent nucleoli.

question: The autobiography 'Wings of Fire' chronicles the life of which notable Indian personality?
solution_text:
The correct answer is APJ Abdul Kalam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Wings of Fire" (1999) is the autobiography of Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, co-authored with Arun Tiwari. It chronicles his journey from Rameswaram to becoming India's "Missile Man" and later the 11th President of India (2002–2007). (विंग्स ऑफ फायर — डॉ. ए.पी.जे. अब्दुल कलाम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Dr. Kalam played a key role in India's SLV-III, the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (Agni, Prithvi) and the Pokhran-II nuclear tests (1998); he received the Bharat Ratna in 1997.

• His other books: India 2020, Ignited Minds, My Journey, Turning Points.

• Books by others: Kiran Bedi — "I Dare"; Arundhati Roy — "The God of Small Things" (Booker Prize 1997).

NOTE

• Dr. Kalam was called the "People's President"; his birthday, 15 October, is observed as World Students' Day.

question: Which of the following revolutionaries, who was arrested in Lahore conspiracy case by the British Government of India, was martyred in the hunger strike of 63 days in jail?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jatindra Nath Das.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jatindra Nath Das (Jatin Das), arrested in the Lahore Conspiracy Case (1929), died as a martyr in Lahore jail on 13 September 1929 after a historic hunger strike of 63 days, undertaken to protest against the inhuman treatment of political prisoners. (जतींद्र नाथ दास — 63 दिन की भूख हड़ताल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The hunger strike was launched along with Bhagat Singh and other HSRA revolutionaries demanding that political prisoners be treated as such, not as ordinary criminals.

• In the same Lahore Conspiracy Case, Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged on 23 March 1931 (observed as Shaheed Diwas).

• Ram Prasad Bismil was hanged in the Kakori case (1927); Prafulla Chaki was involved in the Muzaffarpur bomb incident (1908) with Khudiram Bose; Rash Behari Bose founded the Indian Independence League and helped organise the INA.

NOTE

• Jatin Das's funeral procession from Lahore to Calcutta drew huge crowds; Subhas Chandra Bose received the body in Calcutta.

question: Which of the following correctly describes the nature of the Indian Constitution?
option_1: Very rigid and difficult to amend
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither rigid nor flexible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian Constitution is a blend of rigidity and flexibility — it is "neither (purely) rigid nor (purely) flexible". Some provisions can be amended by a simple majority, others need a special majority, and some need special majority plus ratification by half the states (Article 368). (न कठोर, न लचीला — मिश्रित)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Amendment procedures:

◦ Simple majority of Parliament — e.g., creation of new states, citizenship provisions (not counted as amendments under Article 368).

◦ Special majority — majority of total membership + 2/3 of members present and voting (most provisions).

◦ Special majority + ratification by half the state legislatures — federal provisions (election of President, distribution of powers, representation of states, Article 368 itself).

• A rigid constitution (like the USA's) is hard to amend; a flexible one (like the UK's) can be amended like ordinary law.

NOTE

• The First Amendment was made in 1951. The basic structure of the Constitution cannot be destroyed even by amendment (Kesavananda Bharati case, 1973).

question: The 'Bathukamma' festival is associated with which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Telangana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bathukamma" is the famous floral festival of Telangana, celebrated by women during Navaratri (September–October). Women arrange seasonal flowers in beautiful conical stacks (Bathukamma) and worship Goddess Gauri with songs and dance. (बतुकम्मा — तेलंगाना का पुष्प उत्सव)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Bathukamma" literally means "Mother Goddess, come alive"; the festival ends with the immersion of the flower stacks in water bodies on Saddula Bathukamma.

• It is the state festival of Telangana (declared after the state's formation in 2014); Bonalu is another major festival of Telangana.

• Festivals of the other options: Sikkim — Losar, Saga Dawa; Punjab — Baisakhi, Lohri; Tripura — Kharchi Puja, Garia Puja.

NOTE

• Telangana was formed on 2 June 2014 as the 29th state, carved out of Andhra Pradesh; capital — Hyderabad.

question: Raga Deepak has been associated with which famous musician?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tansen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Raga Deepak" is legendarily associated with Tansen, the greatest musician of Emperor Akbar's court. It is said that when Tansen sang Raga Deepak, lamps lit up by themselves and his body produced unbearable heat, which was then cooled by Raga Megh Malhar (said to bring rain). (राग दीपक — तानसेन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Tansen (Ramtanu Pandey) was one of the Navratnas (nine gems) of Akbar's court; Akbar gave him the title "Mian".

• He learnt music from Swami Haridas of Vrindavan and is regarded as the founder of many Hindustani classical traditions; his tomb is at Gwalior (Madhya Pradesh), where the annual Tansen Samaroh music festival is held.

• Amir Khusrau (13th–14th century), the "Parrot of India", was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya, credited with developing qawwali and (traditionally) the sitar and tabla.

NOTE

• Ragas and legends: Deepak — fire/lamps; Megh Malhar — rain. Akbar's other gems included Birbal, Todar Mal, Abul Fazl and Faizi.

question: In September 2023, after the retirement of Incumbent Sanjay Kumar Mishra, who was appointed as In-charge Director of ED?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rahul Navin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In September 2023, after the retirement of Sanjay Kumar Mishra, Rahul Navin (an IRS officer) was appointed as the In-charge/Acting Director of the Enforcement Directorate (ED). (राहुल नवीन — प्रवर्तन निदेशालय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Enforcement Directorate (ED) is a financial-investigation agency under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance. It enforces the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002 and the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999; headquarters — New Delhi.

• At that time, Tushar Mehta was the Solicitor General of India, Samant Goel had headed RAW, and T. V. Somanathan was the Finance Secretary.

NOTE

• The ED Director is appointed under the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003; the Supreme Court had held that S. K. Mishra's repeated extensions could not continue beyond 15 September 2023. Rahul Navin was later made the regular ED Director (2024).

question: Balban's rule as an absolute despot led to which of the following events?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Destruction of the Forty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ghiyasuddin Balban (r. 1266–1287), the Delhi Sultan of the Ilbari/Mamluk (Slave) dynasty, ruled as an absolute despot. To make the crown all-powerful, he destroyed the "Chahalgani" or "The Forty" — the powerful group of forty Turkish nobles created by Iltutmish — by poisoning, exiling or executing its members. (बलबन — चालीसा/तुर्कान-ए-चहलगानी का विनाश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Balban propounded the theory of kingship — the Sultan is the "Shadow of God on Earth (Zil-e-Ilahi)" — and traced his descent from the legendary Persian hero Afrasiyab.

• He introduced the Persian customs of Sijda (prostration) and Paibos (kissing the monarch's feet), and the Persian festival of Nauroz, to enhance royal prestige.

• He maintained a strong army and a network of spies (barids), and followed a policy of "blood and iron" against rebels and the Mewatis.

NOTE

• Order of early Delhi Sultans: Qutbuddin Aibak → Iltutmish → Razia → ... → Balban → (later) Jalaluddin Khalji, who founded the Khalji dynasty in 1290.

question: Which of the following dams is a part of the Damodar Valley Corporation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maithon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Maithon Dam" (on the Barakar river, a tributary of the Damodar, near Dhanbad in Jharkhand) is part of the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC). (मैथन बांध — दामोदर घाटी निगम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The DVC (established 7 July 1948) was India's first multipurpose river valley project, modelled on the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) of the USA; it serves Jharkhand and West Bengal.

• Major DVC dams: Tilaiya and Maithon (Barakar river), Konar (Konar river), Panchet (Damodar river); the Damodar was once called the "Sorrow of Bengal" for its floods.

• Other options: Rihand Dam — on the Rihand river (Sone tributary), Uttar Pradesh (Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar); Koyna Dam — Koyna river, Maharashtra; Salal Dam — Chenab river, Jammu & Kashmir.

NOTE

• Maithon has an underground hydel power station — one of the first of its kind in India.

question: Which of the following dances is traditionally performed by the males of three adjacent states - Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhau.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chhau" is a semi-classical/martial folk dance traditionally performed by males in the three adjacent states of Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal. (छऊ नृत्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Chhau has three styles, named after the places where they developed:

◦ Seraikella Chhau — Jharkhand (uses masks),

◦ Mayurbhanj Chhau — Odisha (performed without masks),

◦ Purulia Chhau — West Bengal (elaborate masks).

• It blends martial arts, acrobatics and mock combat, depicting episodes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata; performed during the spring festival of Chaitra Parva.

• Chhau dance was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

• Other options: Odissi — classical dance of Odisha; Sattriya — classical dance of Assam (monasteries founded by Srimanta Sankardev); Kuchipudi — classical dance of Andhra Pradesh.

NOTE

• The word "Chhau" is often traced to "chhaya" (shadow/mask) or "chhauni" (military camp), reflecting its martial origin.
